import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Smallest prime $\equiv 1 \pmod n$

$$a(n) = \min \{p \in \mathbb{P} \mid p \equiv 1 \pmod n\}$$

*References:*
- [A034694](https://oeis.org/A034694)-/

namespace OeisA34694

/-- Smallest prime $\equiv 1 \pmod n$. -/
noncomputable def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {p : ℕ | Nat.Prime p ∧ n ∣ (p - 1)}

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 1. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 2 := IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 3 := IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 3. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 7 := IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 4. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 5 := IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 5. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_5 : a 5 = 11 := IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by decide

/--
"Conjecture: $a(n) < n^2$ for $n > 1$. - _Thomas Ordowski_, Dec 19 2016"-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) : a n < n ^ 2 := by
  sorry

end OeisA34694

reformulations.difference: OEIS defines a minimum of primes congruent to 1 modulo n, starting at n=1. Lean uses the natural-number sInf of primes satisfying n ∣ p - 1 and additionally defines a value at n=0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For prime p, p≥2, so natural subtraction does not truncate and n ∣ p - 1 is equivalent to p ≡ 1 [MOD n]. For every n≠0, Mathlib's proved Nat.exists_prime_gt_modEq_one guarantees that this set is nonempty; its natural-number sInf is therefore its minimum. In scratch.lean I proved a n = p ↔ IsLeast {q : ℕ | q.Prime ∧ q ≡ 1 [MOD n]} p for n≠0. I also proved a 0 = 0; this extra value lies outside the OEIS domain and is unused by all the file's theorems.
